newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH SEPT M2, WITHOUT SPT FUNDS, +14.0 PCT. [corrected 14:50 gmt]
newsitem.headline: CZECH SEPT M2, WITHOUT SPT FUNDS, +14.0 PCT. [corrected 14:50 gmt]

text.p: Growth in the key measure of Czech money supply, M2, fell to a year-on-year rate of 11.8 (corrects from 14.0) percent in September from 13.2 (corrects from 15.7) percent in August, including money from a 1995 equity expansion of SPT Telecom a.s., the Czech National Bank said on Thursday.
With the SPT money factored out the M2 rise was 14.0 (corrects from 11.8) percent in September from 15.7 (corrects from 13.2) percent in August, it said.

Note. M2 measures currency, demand deposits, time and
savings deposits, and foreign currency deposits. The bottom
figures exlude the effect of SPT Telecom's $1.32 billion equity
expansion in the summer of 1995 which was put on deposit at the
Czech National Bank (CNB).
The total volume of crown and foreign currency credits
granted to clients in September rose by 11.7 percent,
year-on-year, compared with 13 percent in August.
The total volume of crown and foreign currency deposits,
including SPT funds in banks, grew in September by 10.7
percent, year-on-year, compared with 12.3 percent growth in
August. The CNB said the average interest rate on new crown
credits drawn by clients in September rose to 13.96 percent
from 13.92 percent in August.
